title: Core VFS correctness & concurrency hardening (3 reproduced P0s + shared_log race + blob GC + real read-only query enforcement)
summary: Fix the reproduced P0s in kaos/core.py: (1) UNIQUE(agent_id,path,version) crash on delete-then-rewrite and restore-then-write (compute next version over ALL rows incl. soft-deleted; wrap write() in explicit txn with rollback); (2) read() leaves an open write transaction that blocks every writer db-wide (commit or sample/buffer FILE_READ events); (3) BlobStore/EventJournal/CheckpointManager pin the init thread's connection — make helpers connection-per-call via a conn getter. Plus: SharedLog atomic position INSERT..SELECT (read-then-insert race on UNIQUE position), mark-and-sweep `kaos gc` (ref_count is write-only today, DB grows forever; checkpoints as GC roots), and enforce query() read-only at the SQLite layer (mode=ro connection or authorizer — the prefix blacklist passes REPLACE/WITH-DELETE/PRAGMA/ATTACH and is exposed to agents via MCP agent_query; also parameterize the f-string SQL in mh_next_iteration). Threaded stress test + regression tests in CI.

votes.why: Every load-bearing claim verified in source, not taken on faith: (1) core.py:291-311 computes MAX(version) over deleted=0 rows against a UNIQUE(agent_id,path,version) index spanning tombstones (schema.py:40) — delete-then-rewrite provably collides; (2) read() at core.py:277 issues an uncommitted INSERT via events.log (events.py:36-40), so every reader holds an open write transaction; (3) query() at core.py:636-641 is a 6-keyword prefix blacklist that passes REPLACE/WITH-DELETE/PRAGMA/ATTACH on the full-privilege connection, agent-reachable via MCP agent_query. Constraints: pure SQLite/stdlib, zero new packages, no embeddings/training/GPU/external services — clean pass. Absorption is inverted: the baseline depends on this layer — the version bug defeats checkpoint/time-travel, the reader-lock makes parked item #1 (storage-scale bench) unmeasurable, and the query() bypass falsifies the isolation guarantee the vault vision sells. Structurally disjoint from all prior REJECTs (those were learning/retrieval mechanisms; this is correctness engineering, nowhere near the FTS vise).
votes.gates: This is bug-fixing, not a mechanism candidate, so regression gates replace an ISA.lock probe — but they should still be authored red-first and committed before fixes: G1 failing-repro tests for all three P0s (delete-then-rewrite, restore-then-write, concurrent reader+writer from two threads) must go red on current main, green after; G2 threaded stress: N writer + M reader threads for T seconds, zero IntegrityError and zero SQLITE_BUSY beyond busy_timeout, and no reader ever blocks a writer (assert via wal/journal state); G3 query() adversarial suite: REPLACE, WITH..DELETE, PRAGMA writable_schema, ATTACH, VACUUM, multi-statement all raise PermissionError, enforced at SQLite layer (mode=ro or authorizer), and post-suite db bytes are hash-identical; G4 GC safety property test: create files/versions/checkpoints, run kaos gc, then restore EVERY checkpoint and read every historical version — any FileNotFoundError on a blob kills the GC design (soft-deleted rows and checkpoints are roots); G5 write() atomicity: injected fault mid-write leaves no orphan file row and next write succeeds.
votes.risks: (1) Scope bundling: six fixes in one candidate — the three P0s are non-negotiable, but mark-and-sweep GC is the riskiest piece (collecting a blob still referenced by history/checkpoints silently breaks restore; the code's own comments say tombstones exist to keep blobs for restore) — it could be split out if it slips. (2) FILE_READ event sampling/buffering weakens the 'auditable VFS' guarantee — prefer commit-per-read or flush-on-checkpoint over sampling. (3) Connection-per-call for BlobStore/EventJournal changes transaction boundaries — cross-object atomicity (blob store + file insert + event log) must be preserved or bug #1's partial-state failure reappears in new form; likely requires WAL mode, which is a behavioral change to on-disk artifacts worth documenting. (4) mode=ro second connection for query() is fine locally but interacts with WAL file lifecycle on Windows (file locking) — test on win32 specifically.

votes.why: All three P0 claims verified directly in source: (1) write() computes MAX(version) over deleted=0 rows only (core.py:291-305), so delete-then-rewrite / restore-then-write hits UNIQUE(agent_id,path,version) (schema.py:40) with a guaranteed IntegrityError on an ordinary workflow — this breaks the time-travel-debugging premise KAOS is built on; (2) read() logs FILE_READ via an uncommitted INSERT (core.py:277, events.py:34-40), leaving an open write transaction that serializes the entire single-kaos.db — the parked demo_storage_scale_bench is meaningless until this is fixed, so this candidate is a hard dependency of parked item #1; (3) query()'s startswith blacklist (core.py:633-645) passes REPLACE/PRAGMA/ATTACH/VACUUM INTO/WITH..DELETE on the read-write connection, exposed to agents via MCP — a live breach of the isolation guarantee the federation/company-vault strategy depends on. Value is concrete and measurable without any capability-delta claim (crash→no-crash, reader-lock→WAL-concurrent, unbounded DB growth→reclaimable), so the SWE-Skills-Bench zero-gain prior does not apply: that prior covers agent-capability mechanisms, not deterministic storage-engine correctness. This is correctness debt under every future feature; it should rank first in the cycle.
votes.gates: Adapted discipline: gates are deterministic regression/perf thresholds, pre-registered in a lock before code. G1 (crash repro): delete→rewrite and checkpoint-restore→write repro tests MUST fail with IntegrityError on HEAD and pass post-fix; full suite (613 tests) green; version numbers strictly monotone across soft-deleted history. G2 (concurrency): 8 threads, 30s, 90/10 read/write mixed workload on one kaos.db; post-fix: zero 'database is locked' errors originating from read paths, assert conn.in_transaction is False after every read(), writer p95 latency ≥5x better than HEAD baseline arm; KILL if single-threaded write throughput regresses >10% vs HEAD. G3 (read-only enforcement): adversarial corpus of ≥12 payloads (REPLACE INTO, PRAGMA writable_schema, ATTACH, VACUUM INTO, WITH-CTE DELETE, multi-statement ';DROP') — 100% must raise PermissionError/OperationalError at the SQLite layer (mode=ro conn or authorizer), AND 0 legitimate queries from existing tests/MCP agent_query corpus rejected; KILL on any false positive. G4 (GC): 1000-cycle write/overwrite/delete churn → kaos gc reclaims ≥90% of unreferenced blob bytes AND every pre-existing checkpoint restores byte-identically post-GC; KILL on any restore divergence. G5 (SharedLog): 8 threads × 200 appends → exactly 1600 rows, positions dense with zero UNIQUE violations. Honest survival prior ~0.9 — appropriate, since these gates guard against regression, not falsify a capability claim.
votes.risks: (a) Scope creep: touches 8 modules (core, blobs, events, checkpoints, shared_log, schema, mcp, cli) — should be split into reviewable slices with G1-G3 landed before GC/shared_log; (b) mode=ro/authorizer may break legitimate internal query() callers (temp tables, EXPLAIN, PRAGMA reads) — G3's false-positive clause covers this but the legitimate-corpus must be gathered before locking; (c) FILE_READ event semantics change (commit-per-read cost vs sampled/buffered events losing audit rows on crash) is an audit-completeness tradeoff that must be pre-registered as a decision, not improvised; (d) connection-per-call in helpers + WAL mode changes locking behavior that 613 existing tests implicitly depend on — G1's full-suite-green requirement is load-bearing; (e) GC deleting a blob still referenced by a checkpoint manifest would silently corrupt time-travel — G4's byte-identical-restore check must run against ALL checkpoint types, including diffed/incremental ones if any exist.

votes.why: All three P0s verified in source (core.py:291-305 version collision vs schema.py:40 UNIQUE; core.py:277 + events.py:36-40 uncommitted INSERT on every read; core.py:636-641 prefix blacklist that passes REPLACE/WITH-DELETE/PRAGMA/ATTACH via MCP). Cheapest item in the queue (M effort, stdlib-only) relative to what it unblocks: the reader-lock bug makes the already-agreed storage-scale measurement (parked #1) invalid if run first, and the query() bypass is a disqualifying hole for the company-vault federation pitch. G2 concurrency: threaded stress (e.g. 8 readers + 2 writers, 30s) — HEAD must exhibit 'database is locked'/blocking from reader-held txns; post-fix zero reader-induced writer blocks. G3 query() escape corpus: REPLACE, WITH..DELETE, PRAGMA, ATTACH, VACUUM INTO, multi-statement — each must raise AND db file hash must be byte-identical before/after every attempt (SQLite-layer enforcement, not string matching); mh_next_iteration f-string parameterized. G4 GC safety: fixture with live files + checkpointed-but-deleted files + truly unreferenced blobs — `kaos gc` must reclaim only the third class, and every checkpoint must restore successfully post-GC. GC is the most dangerous sub-item — a wrong root set silently destroys checkpoint restorability, the product's core premise (mitigate: dry-run default, checkpoints as explicit roots, G4). Sampling/buffering FILE_READ events trades audit completeness for throughput — must be an explicit, documented decision since the event journal is the auditability pitch. Scope-creep risk: six fixes bundled; if the cycle slips, land P0s 1-3 first and let gc/authorizer follow — do not let the gc design debate hold the crash fixes hostage.

title: Eval-harness integrity: verify() P0 crash, tautological kappa, unclosed journal loop, hash-anchored results, probe template (unblocks action-realization re-run, parked #5)
summary: Make the discipline's own tooling honest: (1) P0 — Probe.verify() crashes on every results.json the reference probe produces (KeyError per_query on completed runs, KeyError FULL on the shipped VOID file) and an empty kill-gate list would compute ACCEPT; short-circuit VOID, guard compute_verdict against zero kill-gates, persist per_query per arm. (2) Blind-judge kappa is jq.correct==jq.correct — always 1.0 by construction, kappa VOID gate dead; extract a real independent signal from SurrogateVerifier or explicitly document mechanical-label probes as kappa-exempt; unit-test that a disagreeing judge yields kappa<1. (3) `kaos eval probe verify` never compares recomputed vs stored verdict — REJECT-to-ACCEPT gate drift passes silently and verifying an honest REJECT exits 1; return {recomputed, stored, match}. (4) Auto-log probe runs to ExperimentStore from `kaos eval probe run` (run.py's docstring claim is currently false; the flagship VOID#1 has no journal row). (5) Schema v10: results_sha256 column closing the tamper chain at the back, void_verdict() constructor restoring single-source-of-verdict. (6) Concrete Probe.run() template method + shared make_stub_arms so the next probe costs ~50 lines instead of ~350 — direct enabler for TRUF and for the parked action-realization re-run (parked #5, merged here: re-run fires when >=200 organic action-class incidents exist, on the fixed harness).

votes.why: Every alleged defect verified real in source under a kill-first read: judge.py:91 computes kappa as `jq.correct == jq.correct` (always 1.0, VOID gate dead); verdict.py returns ACCEPT for an empty kill-gate list (vacuous all()); probe.verify() indexes arr["per_query"] while the repo's only results.json (the flagship VOID#1) has an empty arms object; CLI verify never compares recomputed-vs-stored and exits 1 on honest REJECT/VOID while REJECT-to-ACCEPT gate drift exits 0; run.py's ExperimentStore claim exists only in a docstring. Constraint check is trivially clean (stats/sha256/additive SQLite migration). Absorption cannot apply: this is not a mechanism, it is repair of the discipline's own enforcement substrate — the native baseline IS the broken artifact. Every downstream decision (TRUF, skill admission, storage-scale, action-realization re-run) inherits this substrate, so it is a prerequisite multiplier, not a feature.
votes.gates: G1 (falsification): unit test where a deliberately disagreeing judge signal must yield kappa<1.0 and VOID; current code must FAIL this test pre-fix (proves the gate was dead). G2: compute_verdict([], kappa=1.0) must NOT return ACCEPT — must return VOID/inadmissible. G3: probe.verify() on the shipped demo_action_realization_bench/results.json returns {recomputed, stored, match:true} exit 0; on a mutated gates module simulating REJECT-to-ACCEPT drift returns match:false exit 1; verifying an honest REJECT with unchanged gates exits 0. G4: `kaos eval probe run` on the reference probe writes per_query for every arm, records results_sha256 matching the file hash, and produces a queryable ExperimentStore row. G5: schema v10 additive — v9 db opens, all 613 existing tests pass. Kill condition: if the "real kappa signal" design ends up requiring a mandatory LLM/external judge or embeddings, that sub-item is REJECTED and mechanical-label probes get a documented kappa-exemption instead — no silent dead gate retained.
votes.risks: (1) Bundled scope: six sub-items spanning schema migration, CLI, stats, and a probe template — the template should be validated against TRUF's actual needs, not frozen speculatively. (2) The kappa fix may be structurally impossible with a deterministic heuristic verifier that consumes the same label; the exemption path must be explicit documentation, not a quietly weakened gate. (3) The merged parked #5 (action-realization re-run) is data-blocked (>=200 organic incidents), not code-blocked — completing this work must not be reported as progress on #5 itself. (4) Zero-kill-gate guard must map to VOID/inadmissible, not REJECT, or it invents a new verdict semantics mid-fix. (5) Retro-logging the flagship VOID into ExperimentStore must be marked as backfilled, not passed off as a contemporaneous record, or it undermines the very integrity story being repaired.

title: Meta-harness search loop repair: CORAL pivot is dead code, verifier diagnosis discarded, seed/candidate apples-to-oranges, orphaned workers, direction-blind stagnation
summary: Repair the flagship search loop end-to-end: (1) CORAL Tier 1 pivot prompt can NEVER fire — dual-predicate desync between _update_stagnation and propose(); make the fire decision in one place via a pivot_pending flag, persist the cooldown reset, regression-test that build_pivot_prompt appears in proposer_conversation.json. (2) SurrogateVerifier diagnosis is computed every eval then dropped before the proposer sees it (CLI/worker path) — persist diagnosis.json in _store_result, load it in _build_archive_digest; implement or remove the phantom LLM mode. (3) run() evaluates seeds on the full problem set but candidates on eval_subset — frontier dominance is meaningless; compute problems once, pass to both. (4) Worker liveness: persist worker_pid/heartbeat via set_state, flag STALE in mh status, refuse double-launch, except BaseException so interrupts call afs.fail(). (5) Direction-aware stagnation (max-over-frontier is wrong for minimize objectives; regressions currently count as improvement). Plus rationale-preserving extraction (# RATIONALE: convention — the FTS memory of WHY approaches won is permanently empty today), resume() per_problem reload + evaluator rebuild, dead proposer tool-registration cleanup. Follow-on noted for next cycle: GEPA-style per-instance Pareto archive + trajectory-reflection proposer (ICLR26 oral, constraint-clean, 35x rollout efficiency) — lands better once this substrate is honest.

votes.why: All three load-bearing bug claims verified in source: (1) CORAL pivot is provably unreachable — _update_stagnation (search.py:466-477) stamps pivot_fired_at=stagnant at the exact moment the threshold is first met, so proposer.py:215-217's check sees delta 0 forever and build_pivot_prompt never enters a prompt, while search.py:473 logs a fire that never happened; (2) VerifierDiagnosis is computed (evaluator.py:157-175) but _store_result (search.py:587-635) never persists it to the archive, so the compactor's h.get("diagnosis") is empty on any CLI/worker rebuild path; (3) run() evaluates seeds without problems= (search.py:85-88, full set) but candidates with eval_subset (lines 179-181), making frontier dominance cross-problem-set. Constraint check is trivially clean (control-flow/persistence fixes, zero new dependencies), and absorption is inverted: the native baseline ADVERTISES the CORAL pivot as an existing capability — repairing advertised-but-dead code cannot be absorbed by that same dead code. This is reliability-first work on the flagship loop, and every fix is deterministically testable without an LLM.
votes.gates: G1 (fail-on-main regression): a test running the search loop with a stub LLM and forced stagnation must FAIL on main by demonstrating build_pivot_prompt text never appears in proposer_conversation.json across 3x threshold iterations, and PASS after the fix; if it cannot demonstrate dead-ness on main the premise is VOID. G2 (diagnosis round-trip): rebuild archive digest from disk in a fresh process (worker path); kill if digest with the fix is byte-identical to digest without it, or if diagnosis.json absent under /harnesses/<hid>/. G3 (problem-set parity): with eval_subset_size set, assert seeds and candidates were scored on identical problem-ID sets; kill if seeds still get the full set. G4 (direction-aware stagnation): synthetic frontier with a minimize objective that regresses — main must misclassify it as improvement, fix must count it stagnant. G5 (orphan detection): SIGKILL a background worker mid-run; mh status must show STALE within one heartbeat window and refuse a double-launch on the same search id. Scope gates: phantom LLM verifier mode is REMOVED not implemented (else effort exceeds M and adds an untested LLM path); rationale extraction stores author-written comments verbatim with NO LLM synthesis step (else it re-enters the synthesis-as-consolidation DO-NOT-BUILD class); GEPA-style Pareto/trajectory-reflection follow-on is explicitly OUT of this cycle.
votes.risks: Scope creep is the main one: the candidate bundles 8+ fixes plus a named follow-on (GEPA per-instance archive) — if the follow-on leaks into this cycle it becomes a new mechanism requiring its own hash-locked probe. Rationale-preserving extraction sits one careless refactor away from the rejected synthesis class (any move from verbatim comments to LLM-summarized 'why it won' re-enters the FTS vise). Fixing the pivot makes it fire for the first time ever — its actual effect on search quality is unmeasured and could plausibly be neutral or negative (SWE-Skills-Bench prior: most interventions produce zero gain); repairing it restores honesty, not proven lift, so do not market it as a performance win without a separate probe. Behavioral change to stagnation semantics (direction-aware) alters when pivots/CORAL cooldowns trigger in existing long-running searches; resume() on pre-fix archives needs a compatibility test. Worker liveness via set_state heartbeats adds write traffic to the single kaos.db — trivial now, but note it for the parked storage-scale bench.

votes.why: All five headline defects verified in code (search.py, proposer.py, evaluator.py, worker.py): the pivot predicate is provably unreachable (state machine consumes the fire at end of iter N before propose() at N+1 can act on it), verifier diagnosis is computed every eval and never reaches the archive digest, and seeds vs candidates are scored on different problem sets — making every historical mh frontier with eval_subset_size set untrustworthy. This is measurement-integrity repair of the instrument the falsifiable-eval discipline itself runs on, not a new mechanism, so the SWE-Skills-Bench zero-gain prior does not apply: every gate is a deterministic assertion whose baseline arm (current code) provably fails, not an uplift bet. Restoring honesty of the flagship loop is prerequisite to trusting any future probe that uses mh_search.
votes.gates: Per-fix gates, each with baseline = current HEAD which must FAIL (falsification self-test built in): G1 pivot-liveness — stub proposer + forced non-improving results, threshold=2: build_pivot_prompt marker appears in proposer prompt at iteration threshold+1 and re-fires only after a full cooldown window; baseline emits 0 occurrences or gate is void. G2 frontier-homogeneity — with eval_subset_size=k<|search_set|, every scores.json records a problem-set hash and all harnesses in one frontier share it; baseline mixes hashes. G5 direction-correctness — minimize-objective stub with monotonically regressing scores: stagnant counter increments every iteration (baseline resets via abs-delta). G6 no-regression — 613 tests green + fixed-seed mh smoke on text_classify with stub provider produces identical-or-larger valid frontier. All gates LLM-free and deterministic; prior probability of survival ~0.85 since they assert verified control-flow facts, not uplift.

(2) Scope creep: the GEPA-style per-instance Pareto archive + trajectory-reflection proposer named in the summary is a NEW mechanism that faces the SWE-Skills-Bench negative prior and must get its own pre-registered probe — it must not ship inside this repair. (3) The rationale-preserving extraction and diagnosis-to-proposer wiring are persistence fixes whose downstream benefit (better proposals) is unproven — if anyone later claims search-quality uplift from them, that claim needs a separate uplift-gated probe. title: Close the plasticity loops: MCP feeds nothing, deprecated skills never die, consolidation duplicates forever, hits have no negative signal
summary: Four unclosed loops, one candidate: (1) the 58-tool MCP surface never passes record_hits/rank/agent_id — memory_hits stays empty, Hebbian association rebuild finds nothing, promotions can never fire from agent activity; default record_hits=True with requesting_agent_id, thread agent_id through skill_apply/skill_outcome schemas. (2) Deprecated skills are never filtered from search/list/get/stats (Skill dataclass lacks the field) — prune/merge is cosmetic; default-exclude with include_deprecated escape hatch + FTS row removal. (3) Consolidation re-proposes the same candidates every 100 completions and --apply duplicates promoted skills every run; dedupe at find time, upsert pending proposals keyed on (kind, targets), honor rejected merge pairs, idempotency tests. (4) Rank-blind rich-get-richer hits: discount by stored-but-never-read rank_pos, add memory_feedback(memory_id, useful) mirroring skill outcomes, distinct-query counts for the promotion threshold. Plus the ISA friction pair: return isc_ids from ideal_state_create and add an ideal_state_record_skill_outcome MCP tool so the finest quality signal in the system is reachable from the primary agent surface.

Constraint check passes cleanly: counting + SQL filtering + FTS row maintenance, no embeddings/training/GPU/external services, and no FTS-vise exposure (no abstraction retrieval involved). votes.gates: G1 (loop closure): integration test — an MCP-driven session issuing N agent_memory_search calls produces >0 memory_hits rows with correct agent_id and rank_pos; pre-fix baseline provably produces 0 (this doubles as the falsification self-test: revert the wiring, gate must fire). G2 (deprecation): create skill, deprecate via consolidation, assert absent from skill search/list/get/stats and FTS index unless include_deprecated=True; assert Wilson-ranking and stats totals exclude it. G3 (idempotency): run dream consolidation --apply twice on identical state; second run must produce zero new proposals, zero duplicate promoted skills, and honor previously rejected merge pairs (row-count equality assertion). title: Statistical rigor for kill gates: pre-registered multi-run variance protocol + anytime-valid e-process gates
summary: Harden verdict integrity itself. (a) Multi-run protocol (arXiv:2602.07150 + Don't Pass@k): ISA.lock.json gains mandatory fields for runs-per-condition from a power analysis, interval procedure (frequentist CI or Beta-Binomial credible interval), and the rule 'gate fires only if intervals separate'; verdict is VOID if the power budget wasn't met. 60k-trajectory evidence shows single-run pass@1 varies 2.2-6.0pp even at temp 0 — inside the margin of some past gates. (b) E-valuator e-processes (arXiv:2512.03109): wrap verifier scores in a supermartingale so probes may stop EARLY on strong evidence with provable false-alarm control — the no-peeking discipline made mathematically airtight — plus online derailment flagging for long mh_search runs. ~100-200 lines each in stats.py/manifest.py; adaptive Bayesian allocation mitigates the k-times run cost. Deferred from this bundle on slot/cost grounds: A-BB bias-bounded judging (revisit if any probe adopts an LLM judge) and BenchGuard task-validity audit (adopt as a pre-lock checklist step, not code, this cycle).

votes.why: Survives every kill under my lens with code-level confirmation: kaos/eval/harness/stats.py's bootstrap_diff_ci is the ONLY inferential statistic in the harness and it resamples queries within a single run — structurally blind to the run-to-run variance component (2.2-6.0pp at temp 0) this candidate targets, so it is NOT absorbed by the native baseline; it is pure stdlib-implementable statistics (no embeddings/training/GPU/external service/new packages); and it is in a different structural class from the FTS-vise (touches no retrieval path — it hardens the verdict machinery itself). Given KAOS's actual product is its 8-for-8 REJECT/VOID record, tightening the inference behind those verdicts is upgrading the load-bearing component, and its self-test is fully simulation-based (zero LLM cost to falsify).
votes.gates: Pre-registerable, all simulation-only (no LLM spend): G0 sanity/calibration — on synthetic null (two arms, identical Bernoulli p, 1000 simulated probes) the interval-separation gate fires in <= alpha + tolerance (e.g. <=6.5% at nominal 5%); G1 kill/power — injected true effect at the pre-registered size fires the gate in >= pre-registered power (e.g. >=80%) of simulations; G2 kill/anytime-validity — e-process with optional stopping checked at EVERY step under the null keeps cumulative false-alarm <= alpha over 10k trajectories (empirical Ville's inequality); G3 kill/cost — adaptive allocation achieves the G1 power with expected total runs <= a pre-registered budget multiplier over fixed-k (else the protocol is unaffordable and REJECT); G4 sanity/determinism-escape — a provably deterministic arm (byte-identical repeat) is assigned runs=1 by the power analysis, so deterministic probes pay zero extra cost. Falsification self-test: a deliberately broken e-process (wrong martingale normalization) must fail G2 — a gate suite that cannot detect a miscalibrated e-process is INADMISSIBLE.
votes.risks: (1) E-process implementation subtlety: a wrong supermartingale gives mathematically-dressed false confidence — worse than honest single-run humility; G2 must be adversarial (include a known-broken variant that must fail). (2) k-times LLM cost on real probes raises the cost floor of running ANY probe, which could quietly discourage probing at all — the determinism escape hatch (G4) and adaptive allocation are load-bearing, not optional. (3) The VOID-if-underpowered rule could void otherwise-informative future probes on budget technicalities; the lock schema needs an explicit pre-registered degraded mode. (4) Retroactive-doubt hazard: the candidate's own rationale implies some past REJECT margins were inside single-run noise — guard against re-litigating closed REJECTs (especially synthesis-as-consolidation's DO-NOT-BUILD, which rests on a structural argument, not a margin) without new organic data. (5) Scope discipline: A-BB and BenchGuard are correctly deferred; if they creep back in, effort M becomes L.

votes.why: KAOS's product since v0.7 is its verdicts (8 evaluated, 0 shipped), and the current instrument — verified in stats.py — bootstraps only within a single run per condition, making run-to-run variance (documented 2.2-6.0pp at temp 0) invisible to every past kill gate; hardening the instrument is the highest-leverage spend available, the SWE-Skills-Bench zero-gain prior does not apply because this is measurement calibration not an agent capability, and uniquely among candidates its kill gates are pure simulations verifiable at zero LLM cost.
votes.gates: Split the bundle: (a) multi-run variance protocol, (b) e-processes, each with its own gates, all simulation-only (no LLM spend). G0 sanity: same seed => byte-identical intervals and verdict (reproducibility, non-kill). G1 kill (type-I calibration): 1000 synthetic null arm-pairs (identical Bernoulli p, n matching a typical probe manifest) must fire the interval-separation gate at rate <= alpha+1pp (<=6% at alpha=0.05); the e-process variant must hold this under peeking at EVERY interim step, not just at the end. G2 kill (power honesty): injected true effect at the pre-registered size (e.g. +10pp on p=0.5, k from the manifest's power analysis) must fire in >=80% of 1000 simulations; failure means the power-analysis field is miscalibrated => REJECT (a). G3 kill for (b) only: at the true-effect size, e-process early stopping must save >=30% median LLM runs vs fixed-n at equal empirical error rates in simulation, else drop (b) and ship only (a) — anytime-validity without cost savings is complexity with no value. G4 diagnostic (non-kill, the value receipt): re-analyze logged verdicts in the experiments journal under the multi-run protocol and report how many past gate margins fall inside the run-variance band. Pre-register k-cost ceiling: if power analysis demands >8 runs/condition for a 5pp effect at typical probe n, verdict on (a) is VOID-by-budget, not retune.
votes.risks: 1) Probe-cost inflation: k-times LLM runs per condition could make probes 5-10x more expensive and erode the run-every-candidate discipline; adaptive allocation is itself unvalidated complexity. 2) Power-budget VOID interacts badly with organic-data-starved probes (action-realization is already VOID on data scarcity; this raises its bar further). 3) A subtle e-process bug silently destroys the 'provable false-alarm control' claim — G1-under-peeking must be treated as the falsification self-test, not skipped as obvious. 4) The G4 retro-audit may show past REJECT margins were inside single-run noise, reopening closed candidates; flagship DO-NOT-BUILD (FTS-vise) is structural and safe, but marginal REJECTs (e.g. HASP absorption deltas) may need re-statement. 5) Scope creep: the deferred A-BB judging and BenchGuard items must stay deferred; the bundle is only M-effort if it stays two features.

votes.why: The REJECT/VOID verdicts are KAOS's actual product, and the current inference layer has a verified structural gap: bootstrap_diff_ci (stats.py, the ONLY inferential statistic any gate uses) resamples queries within a single run and is blind to across-run variance, while external evidence shows single-run pass@1 jitter of 2.2-6.0pp at temp 0 — comparable to margins past gates fired on. This is a multiplier on every future probe (TRUF, action-realization rerun, federation mechanisms) at low code risk (~200-400 additive lines in a ~100-line module cluster, no schema-breaking changes to the 613-test surface). It must sequence BEFORE the TRUF probe runs or TRUF inherits the soft spot. The one real cost — k-times LLM runs per probe threatening to make the discipline too expensive to follow — is gateable, and the 'measure first' objection collapses because the measurement (retro-analysis of stored arm labels from past probes) is nearly free and belongs inside the probe itself as G0.
votes.gates: Pre-register two separable sub-verdicts (a: multi-run protocol, b: e-process) in one lock so (b) can die without killing (a). G0 (sanity, VOID if fail): retro-compute across-run variance from at least one past probe's stored arm labels OR one condition rerun k=5; if measured run-level SD is <0.5pp the premise is void. G1 (kill, false-alarm): on >=200 simulated null probes (true effect 0), the new interval-separation rule fires in <=alpha (5%) of cases; a gate that kills null features is inadmissible in reverse — a gate that ACCEPTS nulls >5% kills the mechanism. G2 (kill, power): injected effect at the pre-registered minimum detectable size is detected in >=80% of simulations within the declared run budget; else the power-analysis field is theater. G3 (kill, cost — the cost-lens gate): adaptive allocation replayed on a real past probe's data achieves target power at <=2x the single-run LLM-call budget; if >3x with no realized early stop, REJECT (b) and ship (a) only with k fixed at the G2 minimum. G4 (kill, scoped to b): e-process on simulated null streams keeps ever-crossing false-alarm <=alpha AND mean stopping time on true-effect streams <=0.7x fixed-n; if early stopping never pays, the supermartingale is complexity without return — kill (b), keep (a). G5 (diagnostic, non-kill): report whether any historical verdict flips under re-analysis; flips are informative, not gating.
votes.risks: 1) Cost spiral: k-times LLM runs per probe could make probes rare enough that the discipline gets bypassed informally — the exact opposite of the intent; G3 exists to catch this but adaptive-allocation savings are simulated, not guaranteed on real workloads. 2) Subtle e-process math errors produce mathematically-dressed false confidence, which is worse than honest single-run humility; the supermartingale half needs its own falsification (G4) and should be droppable. 3) Bundling risk: two mechanisms under one candidate muddies the ACCEPT/REJECT semantics unless sub-verdicts are gate-separable in the lock. 4) Scope creep back toward the deferred A-BB and BenchGuard items mid-implementation. 5) Retro-analysis (G5) may reveal a past REJECT was noise — organizationally awkward, but per the reliability-first ethos that is a finding, not a failure; the risk is the temptation to relitigate closed verdicts rather than just tightening future ones.

title: Federation package layer: APS-aligned .kaos-pkg with Ed25519 signing, OASF capability taxonomy, and tool-description hash pinning (parked #2)
summary: Build the parked kaos pkg export/install layer with the 2026 threat model designed in from line one. Format: align the .kaos-pkg manifest with APS v0.1 (agent.yaml metadata/interface/runtime + digests + provenance block) rather than inventing bespoke — implement natively in kaos/, do NOT depend on apstool. Signing: local Ed25519 default (no external service); sigstore keyless as an OPTIONAL backend only (mandatory Fulcio/Rekor would violate local-first). Capability vocabulary: adopt the OASF taxonomy for capability declarations, indexed via existing FTS5 so `kaos pkg search` resolves by BM25 over structured fields — record schema only, NOT the AGNTCY P2P directory service. Poisoning defense (CSA best practices + ClawHub/Postmark incidents): sha256-pin every tool name+description+schema, verify at install AND session start (rug-pull = hard fail); declared capability scope enforced by the runner; optionally bundle a falsifiable probe manifest per package — KAOS's hash-lock discipline as the registry differentiator no other registry has. Phase-2 items noted, not built this cycle: A2A v1.0 endpoint adapter (the cross-installation transport; raw-httpx JSON-RPC, opt-in serving) and ANS-style naming/resolution (skip its ZKP component) — both constraint-clean, both sequenced behind the package layer they would name and transport. MCP 2026-07-28 Tasks-extension compliance also deferred until the final spec lands (~3 weeks).

votes.why: Constraint-clean by construction and not absorbed: grep confirms zero signing/verification/pinning/capability-scope code in kaos/ (only a raw `kaos export` to a standalone .db at cli/main.py:734, which is plumbing, not trust). The FTS5/BM25 discovery is over a controlled OASF taxonomy of declared structured fields — exact-vocabulary lexical search, structurally outside the FTS-without-embeddings vise (which killed abstraction retrieval, not metadata lookup). It is parked item #2 and literally the stated strategic goal; the two real constraint hazards (sigstore's Fulcio/Rekor dependency, registry-required distribution) are both avoidable and gate-enforceable rather than inherent.
votes.gates: G1 offline round-trip: export→install→verify→run with network fully disabled must pass end-to-end; any mandatory network call = KILL (enforces local-first, kills hidden sigstore/registry coupling). G2 tamper: flip 1 byte in any blob or 1 char in any tool description/schema → install hard-fails; any tamper surviving verify = KILL. G3 rug-pull: mutate a tool description AFTER install → session-start pin check hard-fails before first tool call; miss = KILL. G4 scope escape: packaged agent invoking a tool outside its declared OASF capability scope is blocked by the runner; any escape = KILL. G5 dependency closure: no litellm, no openai SDK, no apstool, no AGNTCY SDK, no embedding lib; sigstore backend must be lazy-imported and absent from default install = KILL on violation. G6 unsigned-policy: with signing policy enabled, unsigned or wrong-key package refused at install AND at load. Falsification self-test: a deliberately backdoored package (modified tool description, valid-looking manifest) MUST emit KILL under G2/G3 — if the harness accepts it, the harness is inadmissible. Hash-lock the gate manifest per PR-2/PR-4 before writing kaos/pkg/.
votes.risks: (1) Sigstore optionality erosion — one convenience shortcut making Fulcio/Rekor the easy path converts this into an external-service dependency; G1/G5 must run in CI permanently, not once. (2) Registry creep — 'self-hostable' quietly becoming 'required' violates local-first; filesystem/git must remain the fully functional default distribution. (3) APS v0.1 and OASF are young specs; churn could force manifest-format breaks — version-stamp the manifest and own the schema natively. (4) Partial absorption optics: `kaos export` already exists, so the deliverable must be measured as the trust layer (sign/pin/verify/scope), or this risks a HASP-style 'already had it' postmortem. (5) L effort with phase-2 temptation (A2A, ANS) — scope must be frozen at the package layer this cycle. (6) Key management UX: lost/rotated Ed25519 keys need a defined re-signing story or team adoption stalls.

votes.why: This is enabling infrastructure, not a capability mechanism — the SWE-Skills-Bench zero-gain prior that killed HASP and friends does not apply to its core value claim, because the value is a currently-impossible workflow (cross-installation export/install with tamper/rug-pull detection and scope enforcement) with deterministic, binary-testable properties that nothing in the native baseline touches. It is also the only candidate that directly instantiates the author's stated strategic goal (company vault / federation), it is already-earned parked work (#2), and the constraint check is genuinely clean (local Ed25519 default, sigstore opt-in, FTS5/BM25 discovery, no external service). The value that CANNOT be pre-gated is the payload — SWE-Skills-Bench says shared agent capabilities mostly add zero gain — so justification is conditional on shipping only the export/install/verify slice this cycle and pre-registering a post-ship adoption gate before any registry/service work.
votes.gates: G1 round-trip fidelity: export agent (files+skills+memory refs) from db1, install into fresh db2; blob sha256 set and manifest digests must be identical and the bundled probe manifest (if present) must pass on the receiving side — kill on any divergence. G2 tamper/rug-pull: adversarial corpus of >=20 mutations (1-byte flips in tool name/description/schema, manifest field edits, blob substitution, signature swap, description changed AFTER install i.e. rug-pull at session start); threshold = 0 escapes, any single undetected mutation kills (security gates get zero tolerance, not a percentage). G3 scope enforcement: packaged agent with declared OASF capability scope attempting out-of-scope tool calls is blocked by the runner in 100% of >=10 adversarial cases — kill on any escape. G4 policy enforcement: with require-signed policy, unsigned or unknown-key package must refuse install — kill on bypass. G5 adoption (the real value gate, pre-registered NOW, evaluated post-ship): within 60 days, >=2 distinct installations/teams perform >=1 organic export->install where the installed agent completes >=1 real task on the receiving side; failure = park all registry/A2A/ANS work indefinitely, keep export/install as a backup/migration format only. G6 payload-utility guard (SWE-Skills-Bench-aware): installed shared agent tracked for task-success delta vs receiving installation over >=20 organic tasks; a degraded delta triggers a per-package warning surfaced by kaos pkg — this gates the "collectively smarter" claim without blocking the layer.
votes.risks: (1) Adoption vacuum: L effort spent on distribution for a project with one known installation today — G5 is the load-bearing gate and has ~0.5 prior; without it this is beautifully signed shelfware. (2) Payload value undercut by the project's own strongest negative result (39/49 shared skills zero gain, 3 degraded) — the vault premise, not the vault, is what's unproven. (3) Spec churn: APS v0.1 and OASF are young; native alignment to a v0.1 spec risks a breaking rev — pin the aligned version in the manifest. (4) New crypto dependency (PyNaCl or cryptography for Ed25519) — audit required per house rules, and no hand-rolled crypto. (5) Schema growth (v9 -> v10 pkg registry tables) and +CLI/+MCP surface on a codebase that deliberately held MCP flat in v0.9. (6) Scope creep toward A2A/ANS/registry service — correctly deferred in the proposal, but must stay gated behind G5, not calendar time.

votes.why: This is the only candidate on the board that directly BUILDS strategic goal (a) rather than measuring or guarding something adjacent to it, it is already-earned parked work (#2), and the cost side of the ledger just moved: three external inputs (APS v0.1 manifest shape, OASF capability vocabulary, CSA tool-pinning playbook) convert the expensive part of an L-sized project — format and threat-model design — into alignment work. Crucially, signing and hash-pinning are load-bearing EARLY decisions: retrofitting Ed25519 signatures and tool-description pinning onto an unsigned package format already in circulation inside the company is far more expensive than shipping them on day one, so 'do it later' is not a cheaper option here, it is a more expensive one. The tool-description pinning component also has standalone value before any second team exists (session-start rug-pull detection protects the current single installation's 58 MCP tools), which defuses the main prematurity objection. Unlike behavioral mechanisms, this is deterministic infrastructure — its gates are binary security tests, not statistical probes — so the zero-of-eight shipping record does not predict a kill here; it predicts that the gates below will be written before the code, which is cheap. The one cost-discipline demand: fence the scope hard. Phase-2 items (A2A adapter, ANS naming, MCP Tasks extension) are correctly deferred in the proposal and must stay deferred; and the runner scope-enforcement hook is the single riskiest touch to the 613-test surface and should be the last slice, gated separately. Score 7.5 not higher because value beyond the pinning defense only fully materializes when a second consumer installs a package, and the storage-scale bench (parked #1, S-effort) should still run first or in parallel since it is a one-day measurement that could reshape the registry-table design.
votes.gates: Pre-registerable, deterministic (hash-lock the gate file before writing kaos/pkg/): G1 round-trip fidelity — export agent -> install into fresh kaos.db -> re-export; content digests must match byte-for-byte, any drift = KILL. G2 tamper corpus — a pre-built corpus of >=30 mutated packages (manifest bit-flips, tool-description edits, capability additions, signature strip, digest swap, downgraded manifest version) must ALL hard-fail install; one silent acceptance = KILL. G3 rug-pull — mutate any installed tool name/description/schema post-install; session start must hard-fail 100% of mutations, zero warns-and-continues. G4 scope enforcement — adversarial suite of tool calls outside declared OASF capability scope; runner must block 100% (this gate applies only to the final slice). G5 regression + tax — all 613 existing tests pass unmodified AND session-start verification overhead <50ms per installed package (reliability ethos: security that slows every session gets disabled). G6 local-first proof — full export/sign/install/verify cycle completes with network access disabled (sigstore path excluded from the gate; it is opt-in). Falsification self-test analog: confirm the tamper corpus actually kills a deliberately broken verifier before trusting a green run.
votes.risks: (1) Scope creep is the dominant cost risk: 'L' proposals with a named phase-2 have a habit of pulling A2A/ANS forward mid-cycle — the fence must be in the lock file, not in intentions. (2) APS is v0.1; aligning natively (no apstool dep) is the right hedge, but a breaking spec revision could force a manifest-version migration; mitigate with a versioned manifest field from day one. (3) The runner scope-enforcement hook touches the agent execution hot path — the highest-blast-radius change to the 613-test surface in the proposal; sequence it last and behind its own gate (G4), shippable separately. (4) New crypto dependency (pynacl or cryptography) needs the dep audit the proposal already promises; neither is litellm-adjacent but supply-chain diligence is the whole point of this feature. (5) Adoption risk: until a second team installs a package, most of the layer is dormant — acceptable only because the pinning slice pays rent immediately and the format cost is front-loaded by necessity. (6) Schema v9 -> v10 migration for registry tables must stay additive, consistent with the v9 precedent.

title: Counterfactual skill-admission probe: execution-verified program skills (ASI) gated by paired repair/regression counting (SkillGen), on SkillGenBench
summary: One merged probe attacking the hole the HASP rejection exposed. Mechanism arm (ASI, arXiv:2504.06821): induce skills as executable Python programs from successful trajectories, admit only after replay verification (skill preserves success on held-out replay AND reduces steps) — registered as tools in ccr/tools.py, injected into the action space, NO retrieval step, base LLM frozen. Admission gate (SkillGen, arXiv:2605.10999): treat each skill as an intervention — run identical instances with/without, count repairs n01 vs regressions n10, deploy only if n01-n10 >= max(2, 5% of m); thresholds hash-locked in ISA.lock.json. Substrate: SkillGenBench pinned environments + deterministic checkers instead of another self-authored demo bench (removes the self-grading concern). Pre-registered kill arms per SkillsBench priors: B0 = same trajectories as TEXT skills (the arm KAOS already knows is dead — clean kill test; ASI's own +11.3pp program-vs-text ablation says the distinction is real), self-generated-guidance prior (-1.3pp) as REJECT trigger, distractor-skills-present retrieval-realism condition. Skill-coverage metric (arXiv:2606.20659, trace counting over the event journal) reports which library entries no probe exercises. SkillGen's embedding usage is auxiliary clustering only — reimplement grouping with FTS5 or drop it. Dropped from this cluster: ACE playbook (deferred a cycle: slot pressure + the -1.3pp self-guidance prior; its embedding dedup step needs an FTS5 replacement first) and MetaSkill-Evolve (+1.9pp on the agentic domain closest to KAOS — too thin until proposer upgrades land).

votes.why: Survives all three kill moves of the constraints/absorption lens on specifics, not vibes: (a) not absorbed — kaos/skills.py skills are text templates ranked by OBSERVATIONAL Wilson quality (skills.py:82 apply() is string substitution; ccr/tools.py has only hand-authored builtins), whereas this proposes executable program skills plus an INTERVENTIONAL paired admission gate (n01−n10), which is precisely the causal distinction the 39/49-zero-gain HASP prior showed Wilson ranking cannot make; (b) not HASP-class — it pre-registers the HASP arm (B0 text skills) as its own falsification self-test rather than re-proposing it; (c) not in the FTS-without-embeddings vise — no retrieval step in the core loop, skills enter the action space as registered tools, and the sole embedding dependency (SkillGen clustering) is auxiliary and excisable. The mechanism is inherently falsifiable (admission-by-execution) and a REJECT outcome is independently valuable confirmation that even program skills don't transfer.
votes.gates: G0 admissibility audit (before any run): SkillGenBench vendored locally, full probe passes with network blocked, grep-proof of zero litellm/openai/embedding-lib imports in vendored code committed inside ISA.lock.json — if the bench (post-cutoff citation, unverifiable today) turns out non-vendorable, probe is VOID pending substrate redesign, not silently swapped to a self-authored bench. G1 falsification self-test: B0 (same trajectories as TEXT skills) must emit [KILL] — if text skills show gain on this substrate the harness contradicts the 39/49 prior and is INADMISSIBLE. G2 admission delta: net repairs n01−n10 >= max(2, 5% of m) on held-out paired instances, hash-locked thresholds, else REJECT. G3 crowding/retrieval-realism: with K pre-registered distractor skills injected (e.g. K=10), retain >=50% of G2 delta, else REJECT — and any ACCEPT is scope-capped to <=K injected skills with skill SELECTION explicitly declared unsolved (FTS5 selection at library scale re-enters the vise; that is a separate future probe, not a rider on this one). G4 no-embeddings CI assertion: probe run fails if any vector/embedding import is loaded anywhere in the pipeline; clustering is FTS5-grouped or dropped, declared in the lock before running. G5 sandbox integrity: induced program skills execute only under existing ToolPermissionPolicy/isolation tiers; any host-escaping call = VOID. G6 dead-weight check: admitted skill must reduce median steps on replay by a pre-registered margin (SWE-Skills 3-degraded prior), else not deployed even if n01−n10 passes.
votes.risks: (1) Substrate risk: SkillGenBench and two citations (2605.10999, 2606.20659) are post-knowledge-cutoff and unverified — if the bench doesn't exist as described or phones home, the self-grading concern the candidate claims to remove comes back; G0 makes this a cheap pre-run kill rather than a late discovery. (2) Vise re-entry at deployment scale: the no-retrieval design only holds while the admitted-skill count fits in the action space; company-wide/federated skill libraries force FTS5 selection, which is vise-adjacent — an ACCEPT here must not be read as licensing scaled deployment. (3) Embedding excision may silently degrade SkillGen's induction quality, producing a REJECT that reflects the FTS5 substitution rather than the mechanism — acceptable (REJECT is honest) but should be noted in the verdict narrative. (4) LLM-generated executable code as tools is a real attack/blast-radius surface; sandbox gate G5 is load-bearing, not decorative. (5) Effort L with ~6 modules touched is the cycle's biggest build-before-verdict spend; the falsification self-test (G1) should run before the full SkillGenBench adapter is polished to keep the sunk cost bounded.

votes.why: This is the one candidate in the skill-transfer class whose value survives the 39/49 negative prior BECAUSE it prices that prior in: it changes representation (text template -> executable program registered via the existing ToolRegistry, verified in kaos/ccr/tools.py) and adds a causal admission gate (paired n01-n10 counting) instead of ungated injection, and it sidesteps the FTS-without-embeddings vise entirely since tools in the action space are never retrieved. Value is three-sided: ACCEPT ships the first measurable mechanism since v0.7 and the natural signable unit for federation; REJECT upgrades HASP into a class-level DO-NOT-BUILD (structurally reusable, like the vise result); either way the counterfactual gate becomes an instrument to audit the existing Wilson-scored text-skill library, which the prior says is likely dead weight. External SkillGenBench with deterministic checkers removes the self-grading weakness of prior demo benches. Honest P(ACCEPT) is only ~15-25%, but information value is high on all three verdict branches, which is exactly the regime KAOS's discipline was built for.
votes.gates: Arms: B_none = frozen base agent, no skills. B0 = same induction trajectories distilled into TEXT skills via the existing SkillStore/BM25 path (the known-dead arm). FULL = ASI program skills, replay-verified, admitted only past the SkillGen counterfactual gate. Optional FULL_ungated to isolate the gate's marginal value. G1 falsification self-test: run harness with FULL := B0; must emit [KILL] (text skills fail admission or show no paired delta) — else harness INADMISSIBLE. G2 admission viability: from N pre-registered induction trajectories, >=1 program skill passes held-out replay (preserves success AND >=10% median step reduction); zero admitted -> VOID (insufficient material), no retune-and-rerun. G3 per-skill causal gate (hash-locked): m >= 40 paired identical instances per skill; deploy iff n01 - n10 >= max(2, ceil(0.05*m)). G4 aggregate: FULL vs B_none on held-out SkillGenBench split >= +5pp success with McNemar p < 0.05 on paired instances, AND FULL > B0 strictly — else program-vs-text distinction is dead in KAOS -> REJECT. G5 distractor realism: with k pre-registered distractor skills in the action space, FULL degrades <= 2pp vs clean FULL (mirrors the 3/49 degradation prior) -> else REJECT. G6 no-regression: zero admitted-skill-caused failures on existing native demo benches; token/step overhead <= +10%. G7 constraint audit (pre-lock): SkillGenBench pinned envs run fully offline, deterministic checkers verified, borrowed code grepped clean of litellm/openai-SDK/embedding imports — any hit in the shipped path -> REJECT-by-constraint. All thresholds, m, N, k, seeds, and temperature policy go in ISA.lock.json, sha256 added to KNOWN_LOCK_SHA256 before any probe run; log via kaos experiment log.
votes.risks: (1) Low survival prior ~15-25% against an L-sized effort — most of the spend likely buys a negative result; acceptable only because the negative is class-closing, but budget-wise this is the cycle's biggest bet. (2) VOID risk is real and distinct from REJECT: the admission filter may admit zero skills from available trajectories (echo of Life-Harness VOID#1) — G2's VOID exit must be honored without retuning induction. (3) Executing LLM-generated Python via ToolDefinition handlers is a new security surface; admitted skill code must be hash-pinned and run under existing isolation tiers, and this must be in scope before ship, not after. (4) Paired counterfactual runs are LLM-call expensive (2 arms x m>=40 x per-skill x per-arm) — cost cap should be pre-registered or the probe invites quiet m-shrinking. (5) External bench dependency: pinning, license, offline verification, and banned-package audit of borrowed ASI/SkillGenBench code are prerequisites to writing the lock (G7), not afterthoughts. (6) Scope-creep gravity toward the dropped cluster members (ACE playbook, MetaSkill-Evolve) if ACCEPT — those must re-enter through their own locks. (7) Nondeterminism of providers can blur paired counting; seed/temperature policy must be locked or n01/n10 becomes noise.

votes.why: It is the one candidate that can permanently settle the skills-transfer question the 39/49 HASP prior left open — with an admission gate that is itself the missing mechanism — and it pays out on either verdict: ACCEPT delivers the only asset class that makes company-vault federation more than packaging plumbing, REJECT closes the entire class with a structural result like the FTS-vise. Score is 6 not 8 because the expected verdict given the priors is REJECT, making this L effort purchased mostly for negative knowledge, so it queues behind the S-effort unconditional-payoff items (storage-scale bench, verifiable-numeric-reporting) and must be staged: substrate audit + gate-machinery validation on the existing text-skill library (S) before the L-size ASI mechanism arm is built.
votes.gates: Stage-0 substrate gates (run before any mechanism code): SB1 — SkillGenBench pinned envs run fully offline (network monitor shows zero egress) and borrowed code contains no litellm/openai SDK, else VOID substrate and stop; SB2 — SkillGen paired-counting harness, replayed over existing event-journal text-skill episodes, reproduces the known zero-gain result (n01-n10 < 2 for >=90% of library entries), else the gate machinery itself is broken and INADMISSIBLE. Probe gates (hash-locked in ISA.lock.json before the ASI arm exists): G0 falsification self-test — B0 (same trajectories as TEXT skills) must emit [KILL], else harness INADMISSIBLE; G1 causal gain — across m pre-registered paired instances, program-skill arm must show n01-n10 >= max(2, ceil(0.05m)), else REJECT; G2 efficiency — median steps on solved-by-both instances <= 0.9x baseline, else no efficiency claim recorded; G3 distractor realism — with k pre-registered irrelevant skills injected, success delta >= -1pp vs no-skills, else REJECT (mirrors the -1.3pp self-guidance prior); G4 admission volume — if fewer than 5 skills survive replay verification over the run, VOID for insufficient data (no threshold loosening); G5 containment — induced programs execute only inside KAOS isolation tier with no filesystem/network escape in audit log, any escape = REJECT regardless of gains. Coverage metric (trace counting) reported but non-gating. No retune-and-rerun; log via kaos experiment log.
votes.risks: (1) Priors say REJECT is the likely outcome, so the realistic cost is full L effort for negative knowledge — mitigated only if the Stage-0/Stage-1 split is enforced so a bad substrate or broken gate machinery kills it at S cost. (2) Executable induced Python skills are arbitrary code execution; sandboxing them properly is unbudgeted scope creep risk and a reliability-ethos violation if rushed — must stay probe-scoped behind an adapter (per the ac4cef0 probe-adapter pattern) with zero changes to the shipped 613-test surface until ACCEPT. (3) External benchmark provenance: pinned envs phoning home or banned packages in borrowed code would violate hard constraints late in the build if not audited first. (4) Opportunity cost against goal (a): a cycle spent here delays federation packaging and the storage-scale measurement that gates the sharding decision; if the panel funds only one L item this cycle, federation groundwork plausibly outranks it. (5) SkillGen's embedding excision is asserted, not demonstrated — if FTS5 grouping turns out load-bearing for skill dedup, the probe silently degrades and a REJECT becomes ambiguous (mechanism dead vs grouping crippled), weakening the negative-knowledge payoff.

title: TRUF probe with random-exemplar kill arm: does any trajectory reranking beat random sampling? (parked #3)
summary: Run the parked TRUF probe (marginal-utility-labeled BM25 + learning-to-rank trajectory reranking vs native FTS5+plasticity), upgraded with the CBR review finding (arXiv:2504.06943): pre-register an additional baseline arm B0' = random/recency exemplar sampling with zero retrieval machinery — the literature says random OFTEN beats similarity retrieval for diverse contextual reasoning. Gates: TRUF must beat both native FTS5+plasticity AND random sampling or [KILL]; as a side effect the probe retroactively stress-tests whether native retrieval itself beats random — something KAOS has never measured (every prior retrieval eval compared against 'no memory'). Depends on the Probe.run() template from eval-harness-integrity and honest plasticity wiring from plasticity-loop-closure (else the native arm is handicapped by the MCP wiring bug, not by its mechanism). LTR here means hand-featured pointwise scoring over BM25/recency/usage features — no embeddings, no LM gradient training, declared in the lock. Related drop: state-grounded mid-trajectory skill retrieval (arXiv:2606.04391) stays OUT until its GitHub code is audited — 'dynamic retrieval' is likely dense-embedding, the exact MATM-class hidden dependency; only admissible later if the matcher survives FTS5 substitution.

votes.why: Survives every kill attempt on my lens: no embedding dependency (BM25/recency/usage hand-features only, and the one dense-retrieval temptation is explicitly quarantined pending FTS5-substitution audit), no LM weight updates (fitted pointwise feature weights are the same bookkeeping class as native Wilson/Hebbian counters), and it is NOT vise-class — it reranks verbatim BM25-recalled trajectories (precision side), it does not generate abstractions needing token-faithfulness + query-bridging. The absorption objection (native rank="weighted" in kaos/memory.py already does BM25 x usage-frequency) cannot reject it because measuring absorption IS the probe's primary gate; and the B0' random-exemplar arm closes a genuine falsification gap — KAOS has only ever compared retrieval vs no-memory, never vs random — so a KILL yields actionable stack simplification. Already parked as sanctioned work item #3; running a pre-registered probe on a parked distillate is exactly the discipline's intended path.
votes.gates: G0 (admissibility, in ISA.lock.json sha256-locked): feature set frozen to {bm25_score, recency, retrieval_count, plasticity_weight}; any dense vector, LM gradient, or external ranker dependency -> probe INADMISSIBLE. Falsification self-test: FULL := B0 (native FTS5+plasticity) must emit [KILL: G1] before the binding run. G1: TRUF fails to beat native FTS5+plasticity arm on pre-registered primary metric (task-success uplift or nDCG@k against marginal-utility labels, stat test and alpha declared in lock) -> KILL. G2: TRUF fails to beat B0' random/recency exemplar sampling -> KILL (both G1 AND G2 must pass to ACCEPT). G3 (data sufficiency, Life-Harness precedent): fewer than N pre-declared organic labeled trajectories (e.g. 200) -> VOID; synthetic backfill forbidden in lock. G4 (leakage): LTR weights fitted and evaluated on non-disjoint task splits -> VOID. G5 (sequencing): plasticity-loop-closure fix must be merged and verified before the binding run, else native arm is handicapped by the wiring bug and any verdict is VOID. S1 (binding side-finding): if native <= B0' random, file a mandatory 'simplify retrieval stack / demote weighted rank' follow-up regardless of TRUF's own verdict.
votes.risks: 1) VOID-by-data is the most likely outcome: marginal-utility labels need organic trajectories with outcome signals, same failure as action-realization VOID#1 — check label supply BEFORE authoring the full probe. 2) Dependency chain: verdict is only interpretable after eval-harness-integrity (Probe.run template) and plasticity-loop-closure land; running early silently handicaps the native arm. 3) Scope creep of 'LTR' from linear pointwise weights into gradient-boosted or neural rankers — G0 must freeze this or the no-weight-updates line blurs. 4) HASP negative prior says TRUF probably loses to native (expected outcome is KILL) — acceptable, but the panel should price effort M against a likely-negative result whose main upside is the B0' side-finding. 5) The excluded state-grounded retrieval paper must stay excluded; it is the exact MATM-class hidden-embedding trap and any 'while we're in there' inclusion should void the lock.

votes.why: Dual-payoff probe with value on every verdict branch: it closes out parked item #3 (the distilled non-embedding survivor of the MATM rejection), and the near-zero-cost B0' random/recency arm closes a genuine falsification gap KAOS has never tested — whether the existing FTS5+plasticity weighted-rank path in kaos/memory.py (confirmed present, lines 127-214) beats zero-machinery random sampling at all. Honest prior that TRUF itself survives both kill gates is only ~10-15% given the SWE-Skills-Bench negative prior (39/49 zero-gain) and the CBR random-beats-similarity literature, but a KILL is directly monetizable: it justifies deleting the plasticity weighting, hit-logging, and co-retrieval association bookkeeping from the recall path. Constraint check is clean (BM25 + hand-featured pointwise scoring, no embeddings, feature schema hash-lockable), and correctly excluding arXiv:2606.04391 dynamic retrieval until FTS5-substitution audit shows the proposer has internalized the MATM lesson.
votes.gates: Arms: B0=no-memory, B0'=random/recency exemplar sample (same k), B1=native FTS5 bm25, B2=native weighted (plasticity), FULL=TRUF (BM25 + hand-featured pointwise LTR). G1 admissibility self-test: FULL:=B0' must emit [KILL] or harness is INADMISSIBLE. G2 data gate: >=150 organic trajectories with derivable marginal-utility labels from the experiments journal; below threshold -> VOID, synthetic backfill forbidden in lock. G3 overfit guard: LTR feature weights fit on a hash-locked train split only, frozen before the eval split is scored; feature vector schema sha256 in lock (any dense representation -> INADMISSIBLE). G4 TRUF vs native: FULL beats B2 on task success by >= +5pp absolute with paired-bootstrap p<0.05 across >= 20 pre-registered tasks, else [KILL]. G5 TRUF vs random: FULL beats B0' by the same margin, else [KILL]. G6 retroactive baseline finding (logged, non-retunable): if B2 fails to beat B0' by >= +3pp, record a separate REJECT-class finding against native plasticity weighting and open a simplification decision — this outcome does NOT license rerunning TRUF with new features.
votes.risks: (1) Sequencing: hard dependency on the Probe.run() template (eval-harness-integrity) and the plasticity MCP wiring fix (plasticity-loop-closure); running before both land handicaps the B2 arm and corrupts the retroactive-baseline finding — panel must enforce ordering. (2) Data VOID: marginal-utility labels require organic trajectories; Life-Harness went VOID#1 on exactly this pattern, and the lock must forbid synthetic backfill, so VOID-on-G2 is a realistic (~30%+) outcome — acceptable but should be priced in. (3) LTR overfit on small N inflating the FULL arm; mitigated only if G3 split-locking is enforced before any scoring. (4) Scope creep toward the excluded state-grounded dynamic retrieval paper, which is likely dense-embedding (MATM-class); the lock should explicitly name it as out of scope. (5) Politically, a G6 trip (native <= random) obligates follow-through on simplifying a shipped v0.8.1 mechanism — the probe is only worth running if that consequence is accepted up front.

votes.why: The B0' random-exemplar arm closes a falsification gap KAOS has never tested (native FTS5+plasticity has only ever been compared to 'no memory', never to random sampling), and every one of the three possible outcomes is actionable at low regression risk — the only live-code touch is arm plumbing in kaos/memory.py; probe subclass, bench dir, and journal entry are additive. TRUF itself will probably be KILLed given the SWE-Skills-Bench negative prior and the CBR literature, but under this discipline a KILL that licenses deleting retrieval complexity is a reliability-first win, not a waste. Score is 6 not 8 because it is hard-blocked behind eval-harness-integrity and plasticity-loop-closure (running before them yields a wiring-confounded native arm and a garbage verdict) and strategically behind demo_storage_scale_bench, which gates the federation decision the author actually cares about.
votes.gates: Stage the probe to fail cheap-first. G0 (admissibility, pre-lock): >= 200 organic trajectories with recorded downstream outcome labels exist in the experiments journal, verified by query before ISA.lock.json is hashed; else VOID without building the LTR arm (avoids repeating Life-Harness VOID#1). G1 (falsification self-test): set TRUF := B0' and confirm harness emits [KILL: G1]; inadmissible otherwise. G2 (baseline stress test, runs BEFORE LTR is built): native FTS5+plasticity must beat B0' random/recency sampling by a pre-registered effect size (e.g. >= 10% relative task-success delta at the harness's standard significance) — if it fails, emit [KILL: native-vs-random], halt TRUF construction entirely, and open a retrieval-stack-simplification issue; that KILL alone justifies the probe's cost. G3: TRUF must beat BOTH native and B0' by the pre-registered margin on held-out trajectories, with the hand-feature set (BM25 score, recency, usage counts) frozen in the sha256-locked manifest — any feature change after lock is retune-and-rerun and voids the run. G4 (cost ceiling): reranking adds <= a pre-registered per-retrieval latency budget and zero schema changes beyond additive; blow the budget = KILL regardless of accuracy delta.
votes.risks: (1) Label scarcity is the dominant cost risk: 'marginal-utility-labeled' LTR requires organic trajectory-outcome data, the exact condition that VOIDed the action-realization probe — without G0 the M-effort build can be spent and then VOID. (2) Dependency coupling: if plasticity-loop-closure confirms the MCP wiring bug handicapped the native arm historically, run order matters and running TRUF early produces a confounded, unciteable verdict. (3) LTR feature engineering is a standing retune-and-rerun temptation; the feature set must be frozen in the lock, not iterated. (4) The excluded arXiv:2606.04391 'dynamic retrieval' drop must stay excluded until code audit — it is the MATM-class embedding dependency re-entering through a side door. (5) Mild scope risk that a TRUF win pressures shipping a reranker whose maintenance cost exceeds its measured delta; G4's cost ceiling partially mitigates.

title: Pre-execution policy gate + provenance taint tracking + origin-bound memory trust (AgentSpec / CaMeL-subset / TMA-NM / ACRFence)
summary: One security overlay in three composable layers, all SQLite-native. (1) AgentSpec-style declarative rule engine between agent decision and tool dispatch in ccr/tools.py: trigger/predicate/enforcement (deny/transform/escalate) rules from kaos.yaml, per-agent policy table, every decision journaled — KAOS's reliability stack is entirely post-hoc today. (2) CaMeL-subset taint tracking: label values entering context by origin (user / own-VFS / cross-agent memory / tool output), propagate via exact/fuzzy token overlap + FTS5 (explicitly NOT embedding attribution — verbatim token provenance sits outside the FTS-without-embeddings vise since no query-bridging is required), block sensitive tool calls carrying untrusted taint; taint labels become predicates in layer-1 rules. (3) Origin-bound memory trust (TMA-NM / MINJA literature, verified embedding-free): origin/channel/trust_tier/corroboration columns on MemoryStore, staged writes, trust-tier down-weighting at retrieval — the precondition for federated shared memory, since usage-weighted plasticity is exactly what a poisoner farms and dream consolidation is a named laundering channel.
